commits.message:
fix(core): consistent ordering for nan vs -oo

Previously both had the same sort key meaning that ordered does not
give a deterministic order of {nan, -oo}.

diff:
diff --git a/sympy/core/numbers.py b/sympy/core/numbers.py
index d109685df524..c1360a138270 100644
--- a/sympy/core/numbers.py
+++ b/sympy/core/numbers.py
@@ -3439,7 +3439,7 @@ def __truediv__(self, other):
 
     @cacheit
     def sort_key(self, order=None):
-        return self.class_key(), (0, ()), (), S.NegativeInfinity
+        return (1, 0, 'NaN'), (0, ()), (), S.NegativeInfinity
 
     def floor(self):
         return self
diff --git a/sympy/core/tests/test_sorting.py b/sympy/core/tests/test_sorting.py
index d525521f448b..e6a09685c380 100644
--- a/sympy/core/tests/test_sorting.py
+++ b/sympy/core/tests/test_sorting.py
@@ -1,4 +1,7 @@
 from __future__ import annotations
+from itertools import permutations
+
+from sympy.core.numbers import nan, oo
 from sympy.core.sorting import default_sort_key, ordered
 from sympy.testing.pytest import raises
 
@@ -16,6 +19,12 @@ def __repr__(self):
     assert sorted([x, func], key=default_sort_key) == [func, x]
 
 
+def test_nan_sort_key():
+    for values in permutations([nan, -oo, oo]):
+        assert sorted(values, key=default_sort_key) == [nan, -oo, oo]
+        assert list(ordered(values, warn=True)) == [nan, -oo, oo]
+
+

This fixes several issues with consistency related to SetExpr operations (add, multiply) when working with scalars and infinite values.

The biggest change might be that intervals containing 0 when multiplied by and infinite value will generate a nan entry in the set.
